text:
alex: FYI I just posted an RFC proposing a rollforward-first upgrade model for on-prem / air-gapped installs. TL;DR: ship delta bundles + staged verifier + manifest pinning rather than trying to do big dual-image rollbacks. Link: <RFC-1898765432>
maya: skimmed it. curious about the safety nets — how do we abort a bad delta mid-apply? will the agent be able to revert state cleanly? :thinking_face:
alex: good q. plan is: (1) apply delta to a staging area, (2) run pre-start checks, (3) switch symlink atomically, (4) if post-start health checks fail, auto-fall back to previous symlink. stateful migrations must be reversible or blocked.
jonah: what about db schema migrations? those are our usual pain point for rollback.
sophia: agree. we should separate code image delta from migrations. agent applies code delta first, then runs migrations behind a canary flag. if migration fails, we keep old binary and surface rollback ops to ops team. migrations need explicit rollback scripts in the bundle.
lee: plus: signed migration manifest with versioned sha256 for migration steps. agent enforces signature check with KMS. no unsigned migrations in air-gapped.
maya: how big are these deltas expected to be? bandwidth constraints on some customers are severe.
alex: typical deltas we measured: 20–80MB for runtime tweaks, up to 1–2GB for model weights. we propose chunked streaming + resumption and an index-first manifest so the agent can prioritize critical files.
jonah: can we compress model shards and ship as content-addressed chunks? that'd improve dedupe across customers.
sophia: yes, but we must keep deterministic order for applying patches to maintain reproducible verification. content-addressed bundles + manifest that contains ordered application sequence.
infra-bot: deploy-checker: new bundle uploaded: bundle-2026-04-07-001.sha256=ab12...ef90
lee: the verifier needs the public key set pinned. For Private deployments, customer KMS/HSM should be used to verify signatures locally.
maya: what about agent storage for old versions? some sites don't have spare disk.
alex: agent keeps N previous bundles configurable (default 2). if low disk, we auto-prune older bundles after successful promotion. also support a streaming-only mode where we keep no full copy but rely on differential apply.
jonah: operational playbooks? operators will need at least one "fast rollback" path if things go sideways.
sophia: RFC suggests a safety overlay: canary cohort (10% hosts) -> 100% if healthy. if regression triggered, automatic progressive rollback and an alert to oncall with CLI hooks.
lee: CLI hooks sample:

```
# promote a delta to canary
rwood-agent promote --bundle bundle-2026-04-07-001 --cohort canary
# force rollback
rwood-agent rollback --to bundle-2026-04-06-007 --force
```

maya: signing/verification lifecycle: do we rotate keys? how to handle old signatures when keys rotate?
alex: key-rotation story: bundles include signer metadata. agent maintains a trusted-key-list (TKL). rotation is a separate signed rotation event that is applied offline. if a bundle is signed by a rotated key, the agent verifies the rotation chain.
jonah: sounds complex for air-gapped customers who want minimal intervention.
sophia: we can provide an operator tool that produces a one-time signed rotation blob customers import via USB. keeps complexity off the agent but preserves security.
lee: edge case: partial apply after power loss. agent should support idempotent apply steps and resume from last completed file using manifest checksums.
maya: can you add a short example of the manifest format in the RFC? that'll help reviewers.
alex: adding now. sample manifest excerpt in RFC:

```
manifest:
  version: 1
  cohort: canary
  files:
    - path: bin/rwood
      sha256: ab12...
      apply: replace
    - path: models/encoder.part01
      chunk_index: 0
      sha256: c3d4...
      apply: chunked
  migrations:
    - id: 20260407-add-metrics-table
      reversible: true
      sha256: d5f6...
```

jonah: can we include a lightweight local eval harness in the canary promotion so we can run smoke prompts for inference stacks? prevents obvious quality regressions.
alex: yes — agent has an optional post-promote hook that runs a harness against local endpoints and emits a pass/fail. test artifacts are local and ephemeral.
maya: do we plan to support manifest signing from customer CI as well as Redwood-signed bundles for hosted-managed upgrade paths?
sophia: yes, dual-mode: vendor-signed bundles for Redwood-managed updates, and customer-signed bundles for operator-initiated updates. agent enforces which modes are allowed per deployment policy.
lee: last thought: telemetry. even in air-gapped setups we should produce a signed audit blob that ops can upload periodically. includes applied-bundles history, signatures, and checksums.
alex: exactly. audit blob = signed JSON of applied bundle ids + timestamps + reason codes. ops can ship to us for support.
jonah: +1. this RFC answers a lot. main ask: make the migration rollback requirements explicit and add a short runbook for low-disk/partial-apply scenarios.
maya: happy to help write the runbook section.
sophia: I'll add the local-eval harness spec.
lee: I'll draft the key-rotation appendix.
alex: thanks all. I'll update RFC and ping infra-team for a quick review. :thumbsup:
